full_judgment:
2. The facts relevant for disposal of the instant civil petition for leave to appeal are that the petitioners herein as the plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.103 of 1998 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Barguna against the respondent herein impleading the Government as defendant No.2, for specific performance of contract. The plaintiffs contended, inter alia, that some lands of SA khatian Nos.223, 224, 225, 226, 227, 228, 229, 911 and 914 of Mouza-Karaitala and Maitha belonged to the predecessor of the plaintiffs, MA Zaman alias Md Hatem Ali and three others in equal share. MA Zaman resided with his family by making dwelling huts in some portion of his share. Among the above lands some lands were acquisitioned and requisitioned through different LA cases and 0.77 acre land was in Khas possession of MA Zaman and three others. MA Zaman used to possess his 4 annas share covering 0.19112 acre land. Defendant No.1 is a son of his consanguine sister Amena Khatun, who along with MA Zaman, Amzad Ali and Younus Miah, acquired the above mentioned lands by a registered deed dated 26-9-1960 with necessary permission of the Government and used to possess the same. Thereafter, MA Zaman getting his share mutated his name in a separate jama and used to possess the same by paying rents and by opening a separate municipal holding. MA Zaman in his old age appointed defendant No. 1 as his Attorney by a registered power of attorney to derequisition the land which was declared as unused land by the Government and for this purpose defendant No.1 obtained signature of MA Zaman on cartridge paper on the plea of filing a petition to bring the Sub-Registrar to his house. His son Zakir Hossain and son-in-law Altaf Hossain also put their respective signature in those papers in good faith. As required by MA Zaman, defendant No.1 on 10-3-1990 in presence of the witness refused to inform him of the existence of any case, rather they then disclosed that MA Zaman executed and registered a heba-hil-ewaj deed in his favour with respect to the suit land. Thereafter, MA Zaman filed Title Suit No.84 of 1992 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge. Barguna for setting aside that heba-bil-ewaj deed since the said deed was forged and fraudulent one. Both defendant Nos.1 and 2 also filed written statements in that suit. During pendency of the suit MA Zaman died on 3-9-1993 at his residence and the plaintiffs got themselves substituted in that suit as his legal heirs. In the written statement defendant No.1 mentioned some imaginary and concocted stories terming MA Zaman as a benamder of his mother Amena with respect to the suit land and also asserting that MA Zaman refused to return that benami land in favour of defendant No.1 and his brothers and sisters and on receipt of Taka 60,000 from them executed an unregistered bainapatra deed on 3rd Magh. 1395 BS to the effect that within 10-9-1993 he would execute and register a sale deed in their favour with respect to the lands. But in spite of executing a kabala deed MA Zaman mentioning a nominal consideration money executed and registered a heba-bil-ewaj instead thereof in favour of defendant No.1 in respect of the said lands and handed over possession. In the written statement defendant No.2 simply stated that the Government has been in possession of the lands acquired by it. To avoid litigation the plaintiffs agreed to that false and unreasonable proposal of defendant No.1 and decided not to proceed with Title Suit No.84 of 1992 and, as such, the same was dismissed for default on 5-10-1993: Thereafter, on 10-9-1993 plaintiff Nos.l-3 along with Altaf Hossain son-in-law of MA Zaman in presence of District Freedom Fighter Commander Shajahan Miah and many other influential persons paid an amount of Taka 60,000 to defendant No.1 as per demand on condition that as soon as possible defendant No.I would execute and register a kabala deed in their favour in respect of the suit land when the plaintiff asked for the same. But defendant No.1 did not do so on some plea or other and further undertook to do the same as per his convenience. But on 24-9-1998 defendant No.1 refused to execute and register the sale deed in favour of the plaintiffs in respect of the suit land and, hence they filed the suit. 

 3. Defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint. He contended, inter alia, that the suit was not maintainable in the present form and the suit was barred by law of limitation and the suit was hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. The specific case of defendant No.1 was that the land of SA Khatian Nos.223/228 of Mouza-Karaitala belonged to Aizuddin, Tajuddin and Khodeza Bibi. After the death of Tajuddin his share devolved upon his wife, 2 sons and 5 daughters. Those recorded tenants and their heirs proposed to transfer their share by sale to the father of defendant No.1 Osman Ali and his two sisters' husbands Amjad Hossain and Younus Ali who decided to purchase the same to the extent of 8 annas share and 4 annas share each by Amzad and Younus. Osman Ali and MA Zaman decided to acquire the 8 annas share of Osman Ali in the benami of his wife Amena and MA Zaman to the extent of 4 annas share each and accordingly kabala deed was registered. There was a good relationship between Amena and her step brother MA Zaman. Thus the father and mother of defendant No.1 acquired 8 annas interest and Younus and Amzad together acquired remaining 8 annas. MA Zaman was the benamder of the mother of defendant No.l. Due to the death of the mother of defendant No.1 there was a delay in returning land by MA Zaman in favour of the father of defendant No.l. Thereafter, this defendant, his father and brothers asked MA Zaman to return their benami lands, but he did not do so. Thereafter, MA Zaman demanded additional amount of Taka 60,000 since the value of the land increased a lot in the meantime and thus this defendant in presence of the plaintiffs paid Taka 55,000 and on receipt of that amount MA Zaman executed an unregistered bainapaira on 3rd.Magh, 1395 BS and undertook that within 20-1-1990, having obtained permission from the income tax office he would execute and register the sale deed in favour of this defendant. But he did not do so and, as such, there was a further sitting in which the plaintiff and Altaf Hossain, son-in-law of MA Zaman were present and MA Zaman then undertook that he would execute heba-bil-ewaj deed in favour of this defendant instead of a Kabala deed because the latter would cost- much. This defendant paid MA Zaman the rest Taka 5,000 and offered him Holy Quran as a gift. Thereafter MA Zaman having obtained permission of the Income Tax Commissioner executed a heba-bil-ewaj on 20-6-1989 showing therein Taka 1,000 as consideration and making his son Zakir Hossain and son-in-law Altaf Hossain as attending witness and since then defendant No.1 has been in possession of the land. So, the heba-bil-ewaj was in fact a Kabala deed. There was no contract between this defendant and MA Zaman to reconvey the said lands to the former by the latter. The defendants simply got the benami land of his father returned from MA Zaman. So the suit of the plaintiffs is liable to be dismissed.
